source: Non-invasive early cancer diagnosis remains challenging due to the low sensitivity and specificity of current diagnostic approaches.

claim: Exosomes are membrane-bound nanovesicles secreted by all cells that contain DNA, RNA, and proteins that are representative of the parent cells.
source: Exosomes are membrane-bound nanovesicles secreted by all cells that contain DNA, RNA, and proteins that are representative of the parent cells.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about exosomes, widely accepted in the field.

source: define three panels of pan-cancer exosome proteins that distinguish cancer exosomes from other exosomes and aid in classifying cancer subtypes employing random forest models.

source: Exosomes are extracellular vesicles of endosomal origin that are between ~40 and 180 nm in diameter and have been shown to mediate intercellular communication in health and disease (Kalluri and LeBleu, 2020; Johnstone et al., 1987; Maas et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Exosomes can contain a variety of biomolecules including DNA, RNA, proteins, lipids, metabolites and other materials representative of the parent cell.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kalluri and LeBleu, 2020.

claim: Exosomes are present at high concentrations in biological fluids, which is a potential advantage as a biomarker.

claim: The study analyzed protein abundance data from 228 cancer and 57 control cell-line-derived exosomes, representing various cancer types.
source: To identify universal exosomal protein biomarkers for differentiating cancer from non-cancer exosomes, we analyzed protein abundance data from 228 cancer and 57 control cell-line-derived exosomes, representing various cancer types (Figure 1A; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This describes the dataset used in the study.

claim: 1124 overlapping proteins were identified across all cell line studies.
source: To overcome the bias caused by such technical factors, we examined the proteins common to all studies and identified 1124 overlapping proteins (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The exosomes derived from cancer and control cell lines are heterogeneous and show significant variation in protein expression across cell lines.
source: The PCA indicated that the exosomes derived from cancer and control cell lines are heterogeneous and show significant variation in protein expression across cell lines.
evidence: This is based on the PCA analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Only eight proteins from the 12 traditional exosome markers were detected among the 1124 overlapping proteins from all cell lines.
source: Commonly used exosome biomarkers (e.g. CD9, tetraspanins) were examined first, and from the 12 traditional exosome markers (Théry et al., 2006; Kowal et al., 2016; Jeppesen et al., 2019), only eight proteins were detected among the 1124 overlapping proteins from all cell lines.
evidence: This is based on the analysis of traditional markers with citations to previous studies.

claim: Six of eight traditional exosome marker proteins were detected in at least 90% of all samples, with CD9 and HSPA4 detected with the least frequency.
source: Six of eight proteins were detected in at least 90% of all samples, with CD9 and HSPA4 detected with the least frequency (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by the frequency analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The frequency of FLOT1, FLOT2, and TSG101 proteins was higher in cancer cell-line-derived exosomes when compared to control cell-line-derived exosomes.
source: In addition, the frequency of FLOT1, FLOT2, and TSG101 proteins was higher in cancer cell-line-derived exosomes when compared to control cell-line-derived exosomes (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by the comparative frequency analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: 78.0% of proteins detected in ≥90% of all samples localize to the cytoplasm.
source: We annotated these proteins using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA) and found that 78.0% of these proteins localize to the cytoplasm and 13.5% of proteins are associated with the plasma membrane (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is based on IPA annotation analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: 13.5% of proteins detected in ≥90% of all samples are associated with the plasma membrane.
source: We annotated these proteins using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA) and found that 78.0% of these proteins localize to the cytoplasm and 13.5% of proteins are associated with the plasma membrane (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is based on IPA annotation analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Gene Ontology analysis revealed the enrichment of proteins from pathways related to vesicle-mediated transport, secretory vesicles, exocytosis, endocytosis, and other exosome-related pathways.
source: Gene Ontology (GO) analysis revealed the enrichment of proteins from pathways related to vesicle-mediated transport, secretory vesicles, exocytosis, endocytosis, and other exosome-related pathways (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is based on GO analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Clathrin Heavy Chain (CLTC) was ranked as the top plasma membrane protein detected in 99.6% of all samples and 100% of control samples.
source: Clathrin Heavy Chain (CLTC) was ranked as the top plasma membrane protein detected in 99.6% of all samples and 100% of control samples (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is based on the frequency analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The scaffolding protein, Syntenin-1(SDCBP) was detected at a high frequency of 97.9% of all samples.
source: In addition, the scaffolding protein, Syntenin-1(SDCBP) was detected at a high frequency of 97.9% of all samples, corroborating previous findings (Kugeratski et al., 2021).
evidence: This is based on frequency analysis and corroborated by a citation to Kugeratski et al., 2021.

claim: Ataxin 2 Like (ATXN2L) was uniquely detected in the cancer-cell-derived exosomes.
source: Interestingly, Ataxin 2 Like (ATXN2L), which has been reported to promote cancer cell invasiveness and resistance to chemotherapy, was uniquely detected in the cancer-cell-derived exosomes (Figure 3A; Lin et al., 2019).
evidence: This is based on the analysis shown in Figure 3A and supported by a citation to Lin et al., 2019.

claim: Ataxin 2 Like (ATXN2L) has been reported to promote cancer cell invasiveness and resistance to chemotherapy.
source: Interestingly, Ataxin 2 Like (ATXN2L), which has been reported to promote cancer cell invasiveness and resistance to chemotherapy, was uniquely detected in the cancer-cell-derived exosomes (Figure 3A; Lin et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lin et al., 2019.

claim: A set of 18 exosome protein markers are present at a high abundance in all exosomes examined.
source: In total, we identified a set of 18 exosome protein markers that are present at a high abundance in all exosomes examined (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is based on the analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: CD63 and TSG101 were only detected in 33.1% and 45.9% of all tissue-derived exosome samples, respectively.
source: Two established exosome markers, CD63 and TSG101, were only detected in 33.1% and 45.9% of all samples, respectively (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is based on the frequency analysis of tissue-derived exosomes shown in Figure 3B.

claim: 31 common proteins were found that met a threshold of ≥90% in all samples for exosomes derived from both cell lines and tissues.
source: To identify high-frequency biomarkers for exosomes derived from both cell lines and tissues, we examined the overlapping proteins that met a threshold of ≥90% in all samples for exosomes derived from cell lines and tissues and found 31 common proteins (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is based on the overlap analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Five proteins (CLTC, EZR, TLN1, CAP1, and MSN) were detected in over 90% of all cell line and tissue-derived exosomes.
source: Among the 31 proteins, there were five proteins that were detected in over 90% of all cell line and tissue-derived exosomes (Figure 3D). These include Clathrin Heavy Chain (CLTC), Ezrin, (EZR), Talin-1 (TLN1), Adenylyl cyclase-associated protein 1 (CAP1), and Moesin (MSN).
evidence: This is based on the frequency analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The study pooled exosome proteomics data derived from plasma or serum for 205 cancer and 51 control samples from five different studies.
source: We pooled exosome proteomics data derived from plasma or serum for 205 cancer and 51 control samples from five different studies (Hoshino et al., 2020; Vykoukal et al., 2017; Li et al., 2021; Lin et al., 2022; Hallal et al., 2020), which included breast cancer, colorectal cancer, glioblastoma, lung carcinoma, liver cancer, neuroblastoma, and pancreatic cancer (Supplementary file 1).

claim: 46 proteins were detected in all the plasma/serum studies.
source: To account for differences in the methodologies of these studies, we first reviewed the proteins and identified 46 proteins that were detected in all the studies (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is based on the overlap analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The model performed best using 18 proteins for distinguishing cancer from non-cancer plasma/serum exosomes.
source: We found that the model performed best using 18 proteins, where the performance was evaluated by the area under the curve of the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC; Figure 4C).
evidence: This is based on the model optimization shown in Figure 4C.

source: For example, apolipoprotein C1 (APOC1), which was ranked as the top protein, is significantly decreased in samples of cancer patients (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This is based on the analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

source: More specifically, it yielded an AUROC of 0.96, with an accuracy of 0.92, a precision of 0.94, and a recall of 0.96 (Figure 4E and F).

claim: The random forest classifier for cancer type classification achieved a very high accuracy of 0.99 on the training set.

claim: The study collected data from 261 cancer patient samples and 124 control samples from four urinary exosome studies.
source: To test the use of urinary exosome proteins in cancer diagnosis, we collected data from 261 cancer patient samples and 124 control samples from four studies, including bladder cancer, prostate cancer, and renal cancer, lung cancer, cervical cancer, colorectal cancer, esophageal and gastric cancer (Supplementary file 1; Dhondt et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2018; Øverbye et al., 2015; Suh et al., 2022).

claim: 229 proteins were identified as common across all four urinary exosome studies.
